pillar_reactions.evidence: Arrived pre-sold and made the case himself before the rep pitched it: 'I see Trevor and I see his kettlebell workouts and I see how active it is and how it raises his metabolism and it really targets the belly fat... which is, I think that's what I need to take my fitness to the next level.' After the phase-one description he restated the logic back in his own words — 'the most important part in the beginning is getting the form down, because if you have sloppy form, that's the way you can hurt yourself... then we'll ramp up the weights.' He also volunteered the time argument: 'it's like a two-in-one cardio and workout in one 30, 40 minute session... instead of doing two hours a day, do like 40 minutes a day, like that's, it's best of both worlds.'

Agreed without questions and demonstrated he was already aligned: 'No, I'm like, I'm totally, you make total sense, because I'm checking the ingredients on everything I buy at the grocery store... six ingredients or less is like what I usually target. And I already know not to get stuff with seed oils, I shop at Sprouts, I buy organic, I buy grass fed meat.' Notable tension nobody addressed: the Primal Eating Protocol is positioned as the alternative to macro tracking, and this prospect actively tracks macros in MyFitnessPal and credits a macro-based coach with getting him to his best condition.

Asked mechanics steadily rather than reacting to value: 'does he basically, he tells me what workouts to do, what week or what day, like it's broken down exactly step-by-step?', 'how does he track like strength gains? Like what does he do through rep ranges?', 'When is typically the live group workout class?' and, after paying, 'Do you automatically get dropped off of the app after the six months?' He is comfortable with the modality already — 'I know check-ins. I've done, like, weekly check-ins where you do a picture' — so he was buying delivery detail, not being convinced.

anchors.raw: I've had one of my good friends. He is a natural bodybuilder. And I actually would hop every few months, I would hop on his plan. So he would give me like a nutrition guide... to be honest, that's part of the reason why I got so shredded was he dialed me in so well, you know?
anchors.competitor: an unpaid friend who is a natural bodybuilder
anchors.note: The strongest latent anchor on the call and it never surfaced as a price comparison — a coaching relationship that delivered his best-ever condition, apparently at no cost, complete with macro targets and weekly photo check-ins. He never priced $6,000 against it and the rep never asked why it stopped. This is the 'cheaper alternative that already worked' pattern that has blocked other deals in this corpus, sitting dormant in a deal that closed. If the programme underdelivers, this is what he will compare it to.

anchors.raw: I also follow this other guy, his name's like Maximilian Moves... He's also Kettlebell. I kind of see Trevor as more of like an everyday that I can do in my backyard versus like the other kid, Maximilian. Like he does a lot of other stuff that you need way more equipment with. Trevor's more like simplistic.
anchors.note: He had already run the comparison and chosen Trevor on equipment minimalism and everyday practicality, not on price. The differentiator that won was 'one kettlebell, maybe a pull-up bar and you can get your whole body' — useful positioning intelligence.

anchors.raw: I know I can take that knowledge and keep going like that. I know, like, I don't want to keep paying Trevor my whole entire life. Like he's going to teach me the workouts and then I can take that and run with it.
anchors.note: The graduate-and-leave framing is exactly what he wants to hear, and it makes a one-off six-thousand-dollar outlay easier than a subscription. It also sets up the post-payment disappointment about losing app and community access — he wants to keep the library, not the coaching.

anchors.raw: it kind of sucks that I had to, like, put $6,000 down, but, you know, that means that's, like, the pressure's on... as an athlete, the best performance is when you're under pressure, so, like, now, I feel like, I have no excuses, like, you just spent $6,000, you better get your out there
anchors.note: He converted the price into accountability himself, twice, unprompted, immediately after paying. Worth capturing as messaging: for this avatar the size of the number is part of what makes it work.

unmet_demand.want: Continued access to the workout library, video tutorials and community after the six-month term ends
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Access is terminated at the end of the term — the rep confirmed 'generally, yes' — and there is no alumni or library-only tier. He asked this after paying, and it is the one thing he pushed back on all call.

unmet_demand.want: A kettlebell instructor certification he could teach from — he wants to instruct and already teaches informally
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep said 'Trevor could basically certify people in that now', then immediately downgraded it to 'It's on the radar for him in the future.' No certification exists today.

unmet_demand.want: A payment plan or instalment option, asked directly before purchase
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not offered. Answered with 'a lot of our clients just throw it on a credit card and then figure out the payments of the back-end', despite the same rep walking other prospects through Payvo and PayPal financing on adjacent calls. He could afford it either way, so this cost nothing here — but it is a disclosure inconsistency, not a product gap.

unmet_demand.want: Guidance on which kettlebells to buy and what starting weight to use
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Deferred to Trevor's strength evaluation on the onboarding call, which is a reasonable answer. Left him unable to buy equipment before that call, so his first days are idle.
